Dentro del cargador hay una bobina plana: Inside the charger there is a flat coil carrying an alternating current. Every current creates a magnetic field, so the coil creates a $B$ that rises, falls and reverses at the rhythm of the current.\n\nThere is no cable to the phone: the only thing that leaves the coil is that field, which spreads through the air and loses strength as it gets further away.
El campo atraviesa la bobina del móvil: The field passes through the phone's coil
es el flujo que la corriente de la emiso: is the flux that the transmitter current sends through the phone's coil.
En la tapa trasera del móvil hay otra bo: On the back of the phone there is another coil, the receiver. Part of the field lines of the transmitter pass through it: that is the flux $Φ$ that reaches it.\n\nThe flux is proportional to the current, and the constant of proportionality is called mutual inductance, $M$ (in henries). The better aligned and the closer the coils are, the greater $M$ is.
es la tensión que aparece en la bobina d: is the voltage that appears in the phone's coil: the faster the current changes, the greater it is.
Si el flujo fuera constante no pasaría n: If the flux were constant nothing would happen. But the current is alternating, so the flux changes continuously, and Faraday's law says that a changing flux induces a voltage: $ε = −M {dI}/{dt}$.\n\nFor a current $I = I_0 sin(2π f t)$, the maximum of $dI/dt$ is $2π f I_0$ and therefore $ε_"max" = 2π f M I_0$. That is why chargers use such high frequencies: the higher the frequency, the more voltage with the same current. With direct current there would be none.
es la frecuencia a la que la bobina y un: is the frequency at which the coil and a capacitor exchange energy effortlessly.
La tensión inducida es alterna, y una ba: The induced voltage is alternating, and a battery needs direct current. Before that, a trick: a capacitor is connected to the coil so that both form a resonant circuit, $f_0 = 1/(2π√(L C))$. With $L = 10 μ"H"$ and $C = 210 "nF"$ we get $f_0 ≈ 110 "kHz"$, exactly the frequency of the transmitter, and so much more energy is used.\n\nAfter that, some diodes (the rectifier) let through only one direction of the current and a capacitor smooths it, and the battery can now be charged. The transmitter does the same in reverse: it starts from direct current and converts it into alternating current.
baja la inducción mutua, con la aproxima: the mutual inductance falls, with the small-receiver approximation, when separating the coils by 20 mm (from 2.63 µH to 1.52 µH).
Las líneas de campo se abren y se disper: The field lines open out and spread as they move away from the transmitter. For two coaxial loops, the mutual inductance falls with the distance $z$ as $M ∝ 1/(R^2 + z^2)^{3/2}$, and for large distances as $1/z^3$.\n\nThat is why the phone has to be properly placed on the base: a few extra millimetres or a misalignment and the induced voltage drops.
